text.p: SME - European Union ambassador to Slovakia Georgios Zavvos has called for the Slovak government immediately to improve democratic development in the country. Zavvos said the main issues were the opposition's absence in parliamentary committees and approval of minority language law.
- Slovakia will introduce a 7.0 percent import surcharge on all goods except raw materials in the near future.

- Opposition economists said the surcharge would not solve fundamental problems of Slovakia's economy and that it would endanger Bratislava's integration with the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) and the EU.

- Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) said Slovakia had to face a wave of attacks from abroad which were damaging the country's image and its economic and democratic reforms. HZDS said the attacks were aimed at discrediting the current government and spark chaos in the country.
- Parliamentary deputies of the ruling coalition have rejected a European Commission decision not to recommend Slovakia for the first wave of accession talks as biased.

- The Slovak government is to propose paying for up to 20 percent of Russian raw materials supplies with Slovak goods. Russia has repeatedly rejected Slovakia's attempts to pay for oil supplies with goods.

NARODNA OBRODA - The Czech company Inekon is ready to withdraw from an agreement to purchase 51 percent of a Slovak chemical company CHZN, after it recieved only a 41-percent stake in the firm. The Slovak privatisation agency (NPF), delayed for two years transfer of CHZN shares to Inekon accounts and has finally transferred 10 percent fewer shares than agreed in the original privatisation contract with Inekon.

PRAVDA - Opposition parties on Wednesday blamed the government for failure to win invitation to the first wave of accession talks with the EU and called for the cabinet to resign. - The Slovak government is preparing a 10 percent increase in energy prices for corporate customers and a 10 percent increase in heating prices for citizens.
- The paper quotes unnamed sources as saying the state budget deficit totalled some 21 billion crowns as of July 15.
- Three unknown men on Wednesday morning robbed the Bratislava branch of the Austrian Volksbank and escaped with some 60 million crowns, mostly in foreign currencies.
